requirements.requirement: MariaDB is configured and operational on node1.
requirements.summary: MariaDB 10.11 was installed, enabled, and observed active and responsive both before and after the node restart.

requirements.requirement: The inventory database contains an items table.
requirements.summary: Direct metadata queries found inventory.items using InnoDB before and after restart; the recovered table used utf8mb4_unicode_ci.

requirements.requirement: A local application account exists with a generated, working credential.
requirements.summary: inventory_app existed only at localhost with a nonempty credential. The 48-character password loaded from the environment file authenticated successfully, and a post-restart insert/select/rollback transaction demonstrated usable table access.

requirements.requirement: The generated credential is stored in /etc/inventory-db.env with root-only access.
requirements.summary: The file was installed as root:root mode 0600 and later verified as a regular, non-symlink file with the expected environment keys. Its stored credential successfully authenticated after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct post-restart evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete: it captured a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle observations, and recovered service, schema, account, credential file, and application access.
limitations: Firewall rules and end-to-end network reachability were not captured, so the practical exposure of the wildcard MariaDB listeners cannot be determined.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unrelated troubleshooting mutation was identified: package installation, service activation, database/account/file creation, and the mandated reboot all had clear roles. The temporary credential file was removed, and the post-restart write probe was rolled back with zero rows remaining. No failed services, package damage, or abandoned temporary artifacts were observed. The one retained hygiene concern is that starting MariaDB in cmd-c976f3d32377468c left port 3306 bound to IPv4 and IPv6 wildcard addresses, confirmed after restart by cmd-76c6b24ebd7744cd; this is broader exposure than the localhost-only account requires, although actual network reachability was not captured.
